text: The column list and the field IDs of partner_instruction and partner_user, and the seventh field of partner, are not published; the DB story of S9 owns the columns, and this story writes the instruction row with the instruction reference, the case reference, the partner reference, the instruction type, the status, instructed_at and due_at only.
why: No source read for this WP publishes the column list and inventing field IDs would break the data dictionary.
read: Template and Rules v1 R7.3; legacy RWB-E6-031 Data table; context pack S9 ownership rows
confirm: The DB story of S9 and the data dictionary owner
impact: Field-level traceability of the instruction row waits for the DB story; the behaviour of the placement does not.

text: The names behind the legacy identifiers EV-20 and EV-21 are not published; the placement publishes rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1 on rwb.partner.events.v1 following the naming rule of R4, which is the name the wave 4 key asserts.
why: The context pack lists the two event identifiers without names and the placement needs one fact with a name.
read: Template and Rules v1 R4; context pack S9 (events EV-20, EV-21)
impact: The event name may change once the catalogue publishes EV-20 and EV-21; the payload and the topic do not.

text: DP-04 is not in this key's pattern set although the placement evaluates the scorecard rule; the rule and its version are read from rwb-decision and evaluated by this service, and the embedded Drools kit rows RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and RWB-P7-E1073-CON are recorded and not added to the metadata.
why: The plan fixes the pattern set and the story may not add an H row; the rule still has to be evaluated.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-04), R5.7; context pack DP table
impact: The kit is a platform dependency of the build that the plan does not show; the rule version is recorded either way.

text: DP-09 is not in this key's pattern set although the placement publishes one fact; the outbox and inbox library RWB-PLT-TE006-CON is recorded as the platform dependency of rwb.partner.events.v1 and of the outbox row written in the placement transaction, and it is not added to the metadata.
why: The event cannot be published reliably without the library and the plan's H row does not carry it.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-09); context pack naming rules
impact: The library is a build dependency; the contract shape of the event is unaffected.

text: DP-10 is not in this key's pattern set although the placement starts a workflow; the workflow kit RWB-PLT-E1071-CON is recorded as the platform dependency of InstructionWorkflow and of the issueInstruction activity on queue rwb-partner, and the activity name follows the example the context pack's call-type notes give.
why: S9 owns no job, so no Temporal Schedule is involved, but the workflow still needs the kit and the name is a design choice.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-10); context pack slide 12 notes and ownership rows (workflows: InstructionWorkflow; jobs: none)
impact: The kit is a build dependency the plan does not show; the queue and the namespace are fixed by the naming rule.

text: The partner clock of an instruction is the service level of the panel row for the instruction type and the partner type; the duration per partner type is not published and is held as panel reference data, never as a code constant.
why: The legacy story has no timer and R-WO-30 sends the instruction the same day without naming a duration.
read: Legacy RWB-E6-031; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-WO-30, R-UNI-25; context pack (FEAT-PRM-02 panel as data)
confirm: The panel story of FEAT-PRM-02 and the partner and agency manager as business owner
impact: due_at cannot be computed until the panel rows carry the service levels; the contract declares it as required on the answer.

text: The assignment entity of the legacy Data table (DF-WRK-009 to DF-WRK-016) is not in the S9 ownership rows and no default ruling names it; this story treats the case and its work assignment as rwb-case's (P3), reads them on the case contract and writes neither.
why: The legacy story lists assignment as data of the feature while the context pack gives S9 three partner tables only.
read: Legacy RWB-E6-031 Data table; context pack S9 tables; Template and Rules v1 R3 default rulings
impact: If the assignment is a fourth owner, one consumed row changes; the placement writes no case data either way.

text: The data-freshness answer for a stale product is carried as MSG-P1-001, the identifier the wave 4 key uses for the same condition; its text is not in this WP's read set and the row carries the placeholder until the platform message catalogue is read.
why: A stale score product must stop the placement, and no message text for it is published in the sources read for this WP.
read: Wave 4 key RWB-ITG-E6031-ITG (stale product path); legacy RWB-E6-031 message set
impact: The identification is fixed and the wording is not; no other message is added by this story.

text: The legacy permission table gives rights R and U on the two legacy endpoints and names no C list; the placement right C of the API sheet is read as held by the roles of the legacy U row, and DP-08 is absent from the pattern set although a right is checked, so the check is declared per operation and built on the guard of RWB-PLT-E1037-CON and RWB-P4-E1037-CON.
why: The API sheet gives the right and the legacy table gives the roles, and neither names the C holders of the placement.
read: Legacy RWB-E6-031 Permission checks table; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 APIs sheet; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-08)
confirm: The access owner (rwb-access) and the partner and agency manager as business owner
impact: The C role list may narrow or widen by one role; the operation and the right are fixed.

text: The panel and the scorecard are versioned reference data held in this service's own tables, not read from rwb-case; DP-07 is absent from the pattern set and no reference-data dependency is declared, while BR-S9-003 still requires the version to be recorded with every pick.
why: The context pack gives S9 the partner table and the default ruling gives reference data to rwb-case, and the two must be reconciled without moving the panel out of its owner.
read: Context pack S9 (table partner); Template and Rules v1 R3 default rulings and R5.5 (DP-07); wave 4 key (BR-S9-003)
confirm: The owner of rwb-case and the reference-data administrator as business owner
impact: The panel stays with its owner and the version is recorded; a later move of the panel to common reference data would change one row.

text: No source read for this WP publishes the InstructionRequest body or the property names of the Instruction and Partner elements; the baseline fixes the request as the instruction type, the placement type and the rule version, with no partner, and the elements as the identities, the type, the status, the two clock dates and the panel fields DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-006.
why: The APIs sheet gives the paths and the access only, and the wave 4 key records that the request body is not published.
read: Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 APIs sheet; legacy RWB-E6-031 Data table and Endpoints table; context pack REST operations
confirm: The tech lead of rwb-partner and the consumers (RWB-S9-E6031-APP, the partner gateway, the wave 4 harness)
impact: The property names may change in the baseline review; the absence of a partner, a score and a rank input does not.

text: No source read for this WP publishes an instruction status vocabulary; the baseline declares status as a string whose placement value is SENT and declares no enumeration, so the accept, decline, breach and recall values are not invented.
why: A wrong enumeration would reject valid partner answers, and the vocabulary belongs to the accept and result stories.
read: Legacy RWB-E6-031 (no state list); context pack (no list of values); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 states sheet (case states, not instruction states)
confirm: The accept and result stories of the module and the partner and agency manager
impact: No value is refused by the schema; a later list of values is an additive change inside major version 1.

text: The four consumed rows are class C dependencies in fact while the plan's C row for this key is None, and DP-04, DP-07 and DP-08 are absent from the pattern set although the slice names a rule, versioned reference data and a right; the story declares the rows, fakes them on Day 1 and records the absence.
why: The plan fixes the dependency rows and the story may not add one, while the placement cannot be built without the four reads.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.7, R5.5; context pack ownership rows
confirm: The coordinator of the split plan
impact: The build sequence shows four C rows the plan does not; no H row changes and the lane is unaffected.

text: DP-09 and DP-10 are absent from the pattern set although the baseline declares one event and one workflow; the outbox and inbox library RWB-PLT-TE006-CON and the workflow kit RWB-PLT-E1071-CON are recorded, and the mapping of EV-20 and EV-21 to their names follows the naming rule.
why: The event and the clock are real dependencies and their kit rows are not in the plan's H list.
read: Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-09, DP-10), R4; context pack ownership rows
confirm: The event platform and Temporal platform owners
impact: Two platform rows appear in the build sequence that the plan does not show.

text: The error set of the three operations beyond the three legacy messages is not published; the baseline declares 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 with one message ID per condition, keeps the legacy texts unchanged and carries the data-freshness text as a placeholder.
why: A contract with no error set is not testable, and inventing business messages is not allowed.
read: Legacy RWB-E6-031 Validation and messages table; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 APIs sheet
impact: The status codes and the identifiers are fixed; one text waits for the catalogue.

text: The capability area Partner portal is fixed by the legacy permission table and the API sheet; its rights are declared per operation (C on the placement, R on the two reads), the C holders are read from the legacy U row and the guard is the platform capability of RWB-PLT-E1037-CON.
why: The sources give the capability area and the per-operation rights but no separate C role list.
read: Legacy RWB-E6-031 Permission checks table; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 APIs sheet; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-08)
impact: The right per operation is fixed; the C role list may narrow by one role.

text: Partner-facing calls pass the partner gateway (FAPI 2.0) that fronts rwb-partner, while staff screens use the gateway-bff composite route; DP-19 covers the composite route and the partner gateway route table belongs to the edge epic, so neither edge is declared as provided by this service.
why: The context pack gives two edges for one service and DP-19 names only the composite route.
read: Context pack slide 8 notes and slide notes on the partner gateway; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 (DP-19)
impact: The firm-facing read is fixed at the service boundary; its public route is the edge story's.
